title: Investigating the role of AI-powered conversation bots in enhancing L2 speaking skills and reducing speaking anxiety: a mixed methods study
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether an AI-powered conversation bot can improve second-language (L2) speaking skills and reduce foreign language speaking anxiety among English as a Foreign Language learners. The study is framed around a practical language-learning problem: many learners struggle to develop oral proficiency because speaking anxiety inhibits participation and performance. The authors specifically ask whether chatbot-supported speaking practice can produce gains in speaking proficiency and lower speaking-specific anxiety compared with alternative speaking practice activities.

The intervention used was Mondly, an AI-powered language learning platform with speech recognition, role-play, pronunciation practice, and feedback features. The experimental group used Mondly for approximately six weeks as a supplementary out-of-class speaking practice tool, with a recommended three 30-minute sessions per week. The control group completed alternative speaking-related activities designed to mirror practice time and variety. Quantitative data came from pre/post IELTS Speaking test scores and a validated 19-item speaking anxiety scale, and qualitative data came from semi-structured interviews with 13 participants from the experimental group.

The participants were 60 undergraduate students enrolled in an IELTS preparation center in China, drawn from two intact classes. Thirty students were assigned to the experimental group and thirty to the control group through convenience sampling, with baseline comparability established using IELTS scores and demographic characteristics. The study therefore concerns adult undergraduate EFL learners in a test-preparation setting rather than high-school students, and it focuses on speaking rather than writing. It is not a ChatGPT writing-feedback study and does not match the alleged 25+25 secondary-school writing experiment described in the retrieval note.

The authors conclude that the AI conversation bot was associated with significant improvements in L2 speaking skills and reductions in speaking anxiety relative to the control condition, while interviewees also reported perceived benefits for fluency, pronunciation, grammar, confidence, and motivation. However, for the purposes of verifying the alleged 2026 motivation RCT with implausibly large writing-related effects, this paper is not the target study. It is a 2025 mixed-methods, convenience-sampled, two-group study of speaking and anxiety in undergraduates, not a randomized high-school writing trial. Accordingly, it should be excluded from any quantitative synthesis focused on ChatGPT-based writing feedback in high school, and it provides no original motivation or writing statistics relevant to that synthesis.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed controlled pre/post intervention study with comparison group and standardized outcome measures, but it is not actually randomized: participants came from two intact classes and were assigned through convenience sampling. The study therefore has quasi-experimental features with some credibility strengths, but it does not meet RCT standards and the supplied excerpt omits key numerical results needed for full verification.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper claims positive effects on speaking proficiency and anxiety, but the excerpt does not report verifiable standardized effect sizes or confidence intervals. Because impact magnitude is unclear and the study population is adult IELTS-preparation students rather than high-school writing learners, impact for the target synthesis is uncertain.

interventions.use_case: AI-powered speaking practice using the Mondly language-learning app with speech recognition, simulated dialogues, pronunciation/grammar feedback, and role-play tasks for adult EFL learners preparing for IELTS.
Mondly delivered as an app-based out-of-class supplementary practice tool over 6 weeks with short structured sessions targeting speaking fluency, pronunciation, and anxiety reduction.

finding.finding_summary: The paper reports statistically significant improvement in L2 speaking skills for the experimental group using Mondly compared with the control group, assessed via pre/post IELTS Speaking tests covering fluency/coherence, lexical resource, grammatical range/accuracy, and pronunciation. Sample size was 60 total (30 treatment, 30 control), but the excerpt provided does not include the actual posttest means, ANCOVA coefficients, effect sizes, or confidence intervals, so the magnitude cannot be verified from the supplied text.
finding.measure: IELTS Speaking test scores rated by two IELTS-certified examiners

finding.finding_summary: The study reports reduced L2 speaking anxiety in the experimental group relative to control after 6 weeks of Mondly use, based on a validated 19-item speaking-anxiety scale. Qualitative interviews with 13 treatment participants also described increased confidence, motivation, and lower anxiety, but the excerpt does not provide the quantitative anxiety means, standardized effect size, or confidence interval needed to verify the magnitude.
finding.measure: 19-item L2 speaking anxiety scale by Ozdemir and Papi (2022); qualitative interviews on confidence/motivation/anxiety
